description: Signature edition. This entry teaches The Future of Cognitive Psychology as part of the fundamentals of cognitive psychology, presented the Signature way: from first principles, in plain language, building toward mastery. It sits at the Advanced tier of the teaching ladder, where each idea earns its place before the next is introduced. Signature-authored and Signature-labeled throughout.
overview: In the Signature teaching of cognitive psychology, The Future of Cognitive Psychology is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Long-term memory means encoding, storage, and retrieval across a lifetime. Decision-making means the biases systematically bending human judgment. Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Advanced material that follows.
core_concepts: Long-term memory: encoding, storage, and retrieval across a lifetime.
Decision-making: the biases systematically bending human judgment.
key_laws: Levels of processing: deeper encoding producing better memory.
Dual-process theory: fast intuition versus slow deliberation.
vocabulary: Priming: prior exposure influencing later responses.
Heuristic: the mental shortcut, fast but biased.
methods: Computational modeling: formal models predicting behavior.
history: Cognitive psychology was born in the 1950s-60s revolt against behaviorism; Miller, Neisser, and Simon founded it. The computer metaphor organized decades of research, and neuroscience plus AI now deepen and challenge it.
key_points: Long-term memory: encoding, storage, and retrieval across a lifetime.
